source: https://github.com/unreallabsai/unreal-agent - a full clone at commit b7c9bf1 read at first hand (README.md, LICENSE, go.mod, CONTRIBUTING.md, Makefile, Dockerfile, .github/workflows/{ci,release}.yml, harness/{inbox,coordinator,operation,primitives,contextbuilder,tool,sessionstore,llm}, cmd/{internal/agentrunner,unreal-agent-runner}, benchmarks/harbor, internal/openaiapi); plus the live page, the launch post https://unreallabs.ai/blog/unreal-agent/ (HTTP 200) and Hacker News item 49805748 (score 56, 42 comments, read through the Firebase API on 2026-09-22); nothing installed, built or executed
inclusion: the artifact under survey, and the only source in this set that is the thing being judged rather than a claim about it: it carries the three invariants this line borrows (commit-before-dispatch, a version gate at record zero, producer-supplied identity with the dedup set rebuilt from history) and the three gaps it refuses to borrow (the declared-and-dead omission record, the FIXME'd fork path, the uncaptured truncated result), which together are the whole answer to 'what is integrable'
verified: clone at b7c9bf1, read at first hand in seven read-only passes and re-checked by the session at the cited lines
the live repository page, the launch post and HN item 49805748, independent of the clone
quality: Grey: a project's own README, code and launch post plus an unmoderated launch thread. The code and the MIT licence are read first-hand and are checkable; the star and fork counts come from a rendered page because api.github.com was rate-limited. CONTRIBUTING.md states the repository 'contains selected components from a larger internal codebase' and does not review pull requests, so what is readable is a published slice and not the shipped product. The launch post's four benchmark tables (Terminal-Bench 4.0, SWE-Atlas Codebase QnA, DeepSWE 1.1, ALE-CLI) are the author's own and none was reproduced; the top methodological objection in the launch thread is that the headline comparison runs Unreal Agent at Astra xhigh against Codex at Astra max, and a practitioner in the same thread states his own harness has used the approach since February - both quoted as claims only.

source: read through orx: https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2608.03836 (report and body); second record https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2608.03836 (title, one author, cs.LG, published 2026-08-04), 2026-09-22
inclusion: supplies the six-property vocabulary (prefix continuation, effect exactly-once, fork determinism, checkpoint validity, consume-once, recovery determinism) with which this line states which guarantees tezgah does and does not hold, and the measurement showing that consume-once is the property that fails under concurrent delivery even on durable backends - the reason the verdict is to adopt the vocabulary rather than to buy the store
quality: an arXiv preprint by a single independent researcher, not a peer-reviewed venue record; the TLA+ and TLAPS checking and the five-framework probe are the author's own figures and none was reproduced here

source: read through orx: https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2608.22928 (report and body); second record https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2608.22928 (title, six authors, cs.PL, published 2026-08-24), 2026-09-22
inclusion: names the three questions any derived state must answer (in-flight work, already-issued authorizations, results still required), which is what turns the surveyed repository's own FIXME on its fork path into a published finding and supplies this line's one review checklist for tezgah's forked state
quality: an arXiv preprint (cs.PL) from a six-author academic/industry group; the exact checker it describes is not available to this line, so only the checklist is carried

source: read through orx: https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2606.19409 (report and body); second record https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2606.19409 (title, three authors, cs.SE, published 2026-06-17), 2026-09-22
inclusion: the published statement of the design thesis the surveyed repository implements in a narrower form (one first-class state value carrying lineage, pending work and tool evidence), and the source that prices it honestly by declaring its claims limited to controlled runtime properties - which is why this line declines the runtime and takes only the evidence record it names as the thing compression loses
quality: an arXiv preprint (cs.SE) describing a system architecture; its own report states that broad quantitative comparison, live-provider quality and memory quality are left to follow-on evaluation, so no measured win is claimed and none is carried

source: read through orx: https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2608.28553 (AAMAS 2027 camera-ready body); second record https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2608.28553 (title, five authors, cs.AI, published 2026-08-28), 2026-09-22
inclusion: the decisive evidence on the axis that decides this line's answer: it shows the fault-tolerance guarantee is bought by moving components and records out of the failing process into a router and an append-only transcript owned by no process, which is precisely the long-lived process and shared store a daemon-less hook harness does not have
quality: an arXiv preprint accepted to the AAMAS 2027 research paper track; the 200-task fault experiment and the 1/823 bus-hop figure are the authors' own and none was reproduced here

source: read through orx: https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2608.26225 (IEEE-style camera-ready body); second record https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2608.26225 (title, three authors, published 2026-08-26), 2026-09-22
inclusion: the one source whose whole yield is portable to a harness with no runtime: two admissibility rules for a reliability decision (identity adequacy, evidence adequacy), each derived from measured production incidents, which together are the test this line applies to tezgah's own gate, Stop rule and counters
quality: an arXiv preprint reporting an incident study of one production platform (147 numbered incidents over 81 runs); the mutation proofs are the authors' own and none was reproduced here

source: read through orx: https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2608.06790 (report and body); second record https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2608.06790 (title, thirteen authors, cs.SE, published 2026-08-07), 2026-09-22
inclusion: supplies the second, independent reason the async engine does not fit: the retry and early-termination behaviours its fault injection exists to observe are behaviours of a loop that owns the call sequence, so the instrument presupposes the engine, and tezgah's hooks do not own that sequence - the host does
quality: an arXiv preprint (cs.SE) from a thirteen-author group; its comparative claims about prior injection classes are positional arguments the authors make, and their tool was not run here

source: https://stencil.so/blog/harness-playbook read in full on 2026-09-23 through the site's own markdown alternate (/index.md): 2918 lines, nine chapters and two appendices; nothing installed, built or run
inclusion: the design rationale for omp-squared, written by the maintainer of omp - which is one of tezgah's six hosts - so it is both an adoption source and the only published statement of where that host is going; it carries the measured roster-tax figure that gives plan 012 its reason, the AutoQA shape that matches plan 004's open goal, and the version-your-traces rule that names a field tezgah's own ledger rows lack, while its session DOM, Director stack, renderer and TLA+ transcript protocol all presuppose a loop tezgah does not have
verified: stencil.so/blog/harness-playbook (read in full at first hand)
the same author's prior post blog.can.ac/2026/08/03/the-minutiae-of-tool-calling/ and the Pi extension sources the appendix links, cited inside the document itself
quality: a maintainer's postmortem of a system with real users, carrying the author's own measurements (78 extension examples reviewed, 36.6s vs 42.2s vs 37.0s on task sol, 267s to 90ms on the renderer) - none of which was reproduced here, and all of which are one vendor's account of its own product; the appendix links to specific Pi source lines, which is what makes its failure list checkable
